heard: Engineers hand-colored the first photo of Mars using art pastels. JPL scientists couldn't wait hours for computers to process Mariner 4's data. People expected to see liquid canals and signs of alien civilization. So engineers pinned numerical printouts to a wall and painted each pixel. The completed drawing didn't reveal a lush, living alien world. Instead, it showed a dead, frozen surface covered in ancient craters. That simple paper image changed our vision of Mars forever.
